title: Problem into solution
idea: Black Friday (Brief doc tab "Black Friday", #45). Swipe of Mywayup's "Debloat Detox" Black Friday ad: started Nov 5, 2025, ran through last Black Friday and is still live 366 days later. Comment-reply opener ("My belly is too big. What do you recommend?") answered by a calm man at a podcast mic, swapped to our castor oil wrap. Mechanism modeled on Dr. Eric Berg's belly-button castor oil reel (~2.45M views): blood vessels → ricinoleic acid (~90%) → calming, anti-inflammatory → soaks in deep, plus "a lot of women say" framing and "without taking anything orally". Made mostly B-roll (80/20) per our rules. Offer: Black Friday Buy 1 Get 1 + 30-day money-back guarantee even if used.

script.script: You roll our cold-pressed castor oil on your belly before bed, put the cotton wrap on, and just relax for about thirty minutes.

script.script: Here's why it works. Everything in your stomach is connected to a dense network of blood vessels. And castor oil is about ninety percent ricinoleic acid, which has a really powerful calming, anti-inflammatory effect. So when you roll it on your belly, it soaks in deep, right where the bloating is. It's the natural way.
script.visual: B-ROLL (3D, modeled on the Dr. Berg belly-button reel 0:06-0:21): on "connected to a dense network of blood vessels" a see-through 3D belly where the network of blood vessels lights up red (Berg 0:06); on "ricinoleic acid" a golden oil drop macro labelled RICINOLEIC ACID (Berg 0:09); on "soaks in deep" the oil sinks in and a warm glow spreads through the belly, the swollen belly outline calms down (Berg 0:18).

script.script: It's organic, it's hexane-free, and it goes straight from the cold press into dark amber glass. Never plastic.

script.script: A lot of people do suffer with bloating, and it makes them feel bigger than they are.
script.visual: B-ROLL (live action, real women 45-55): one undoing the top button of her jeans at her desk mid-afternoon; another side-on in the bathroom mirror, hand on her bloated belly, sighing.

script.script: So we totally understand. Thousands of women say their stomach feels flatter and calmer, their jeans fit better, and they did it without taking anything orally.

editing_notes:
Replicate this format: Reference (link above). Mywayup "Debloat Detox" Black Friday ad.

A-ROLL vs B-ROLL (every row in the script is labelled):
- A-ROLL = him at the podcast mic. Only twice: the end of the hook line (2-3 s, ref 0:02) and one short nod/return near the end (2-3 s, ref 0:36-0:43). About 20% of the ad.
- B-ROLL = everything else, under his voice, one shot per line, new shot every 2-3 s. Every B-roll shot is phone-real and based on a real clip: real women in real homes doing real things (rolling the oil on, pulling the wrap snug, undoing jeans at a desk, buttoning them in the morning), handheld, natural light, real skin texture, our real product photos (Products tab). Genjitsu on every shot with a person.
- The mechanism shot is the one 3D shot, modeled on Dr. Eric Berg's belly-button reel (blood vessels lighting up red at 0:06, oil drop macro at 0:09, oil sinking in at 0:18).

FRAME BY FRAME:
- 0:00 HOOK FRAME: woman holding the "BLACK FRIDAY · BUY 1 GET 1 FREE" balloon over her belly + TikTok-style comment-reply sticker in the middle. The balloon slowly shrinks while his first words play (VO).
- Thin Black Friday banner along the very top the WHOLE video (ref: salmon strip "Save Up To 44% Off Sitewide"): ours "BLACK FRIDAY · BUY 1 GET 1 FREE".

CAPTIONS: white italic text in light-blue boxes, centred low, 3-6 words at a time, like the reference.
HOOKS: H1 sticker "My belly is too big 😔 What do you recommend?" / H2 same frame, sticker "I'm bloated every day 😔 What do you recommend?". Same spoken line.
OFFER: Buy 1 Get 1 Free + 30-day money-back guarantee even if used (both on the site). Confirm the wrap kit's Black Friday price/landing page with the client before launch.
CLAIMS: no "doctor/clinician", no constipation, liver, lymph or organ claims. "Dense network of blood vessels" + "powerful calming, anti-inflammatory effect" are Dr. Berg's framing; results are framed as what women say.
Doc: Brief H+S, tab "Black Friday".

Voiceover: His own voice, American, calm and matter-of-fact, like he answers this question every day (match the reference's relaxed, slightly unscripted delivery and pace, about 45 s).
